summary: Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen did not run again, so the seat was open. Democrat Chris Pappas won, defeating Republican John E. Sununu.

candidates.name: Chris Pappas
candidates.bio: Chris Pappas is a Democrat who represents New Hampshire in the U.S. House. He won the Democratic nomination for the open Senate seat in 2026.

positions.summary: Says he fought to expand Medicaid and has stood up to Big Pharma to lower drug costs.
Says he wants to invest in renewable energy and is cracking down on predatory companies that target veterans and pollute water.
Says he has worked to protect funding for Planned Parenthood.
Says he supports comprehensive immigration reform that fixes the system and also addresses border security with better infrastructure and technology.
Says he is pushing tax cuts for working families and small businesses.

candidates.name: John E. Sununu
candidates.bio: John E. Sununu is a Republican who previously served as a U.S. Senator and U.S. Representative from New Hampshire. He won the Republican nomination for the open seat in 2026.

positions.summary: Lists keeping taxes low among his priorities.
Says health care affordability comes from competition, expanded health savings accounts and more price transparency.
Says the country needs more energy production, more transmission infrastructure and more pipeline capacity.
Lists keeping the borders secure among his priorities.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Shares refreshed Nov. 25, 2026 from The Green Papers, including write-ins in the total. State certification was not confirmed.
